blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how goods move from the factory to your local market? This journey is known as distributive trade.

blocks.markdown: Distributive trade involves all activities related to the movement of goods from producers to consumers. It includes both wholesale and retail trade, which play crucial roles in ensuring that goods are available to consumers.

blocks.title: Definition of Wholesale and Retail Trade
blocks.text: Wholesale trade involves buying goods in large quantities from producers and selling them in smaller quantities to retailers. Retail trade involves selling goods directly to the final consumers.

blocks.markdown: Wholesalers act as intermediaries between producers and retailers. They buy in bulk, which allows them to get discounts and sell at a profit to retailers. Retailers, on the other hand, sell directly to consumers, often offering a variety of products in smaller quantities.
A simple channel of distribution can be represented as: **Producer → Wholesaler → Retailer → Consumer**. This channel illustrates the flow of goods from the production stage to the final consumer.

blocks.title: Example of a Distribution Channel
blocks.prompt: Consider a rice producer in Kebbi State. How does the rice reach a consumer in Lagos?

steps.text: The rice producer harvests and packages the rice.
A wholesaler in Lagos purchases a large quantity of rice from the producer.
The wholesaler sells smaller quantities of rice to various retailers in Lagos.
Consumers buy rice in desired quantities from their local retailers.

blocks.answer: The rice moves from the producer to a wholesaler, then to retailers, and finally to consumers.

blocks.markdown: Wholesalers provide several services to retailers, such as offering credit facilities, providing storage, and supplying a variety of goods. These services help retailers manage their inventory and meet consumer demands effectively.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: When asked to draw a channel of distribution, remember to include all key players: Producer, Wholesaler, Retailer, and Consumer.

points: Distributive trade includes wholesale and retail trade, which facilitate the movement of goods to consumers.
A typical channel of distribution is: Producer → Wholesaler → Retailer → Consumer.
Wholesalers provide essential services to retailers, such as credit and storage.
